body.statement:
Suppose the oracle frontier \(\{(W(\theta_c),K(\theta_c)):c\in\mathcal C\}\) is nonconstant.  Then there is a constant \(\kappa_K>0\) such that
\[
 \frac d{dc}K(\theta_c)=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\leq-\kappa_K<0
 \quad\text{for every }c\in\mathcal C.
\]
Put \(K_{\max}=K(\theta_{c_{\min}})\), \(K_{\min}=K(\theta_{c_{\max}})\), and \(\mathcal K=[K_{\min},K_{\max}]\).  Then \(K_{\min}<K_{\max}\), every \(k\in\mathcal K\) has a unique inverse \(c(k)\in\mathcal C\) satisfying \(K(\theta_{c(k)})=k\), and \(c(\cdot)\) is measurable and continuous.  On \((K_{\min},K_{\max})\),
\[
 c'(k)=-\{g_{c(k)}^\top H_{c(k)}^{-1}g_{c(k)}\}^{-1},
 \qquad |c(k)-c(\widetilde k)|\leq\kappa_K^{-1}|k-\widetilde k|
 \quad\text{for all }k,\widetilde k\in\mathcal K.
\]
The endpoint conventions are \(c(K_{\max})=c_{\min}\) and \(c(K_{\min})=c_{\max}\).  The clipped extension to every \(k\in\mathbb R\) is defined by \(c^\dagger(k)=c_{\min}\) for \(k\geq K_{\max}\), \(c^\dagger(k)=c(k)\) for \(K_{\min}<k<K_{\max}\), and \(c^\dagger(k)=c_{\max}\) for \(k\leq K_{\min}\).  In particular, the inverse of any prespecified compact interval contained in \((K_{\min},K_{\max})\) is a compact subset of \((c_{\min},c_{\max})\).
body.proof_tex:
By Proposition \(\textnormal{prop:softmax-geometry}\), the path \(c\mapsto\theta_c\) is continuously differentiable, \(\frac d{dc}K(\theta_c)=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\), and the frontier is either constant or has strictly decreasing divergence.  We verify the stronger pointwise and uniform statements rather than inferring them merely from strict monotonicity.

If \(\theta_{c_0}=0\) for some \(c_0\), Proposition \(\textnormal{prop:softmax-geometry}\) gives \(K\geq0\) and \(K(0)=0\).  Uniform interiority makes zero an interior minimizer, hence \(\nabla K(0)=0\).  Smoothness makes \(\nabla K\) locally Lipschitz at zero, while the path equation and uniform curvature give \(\theta_c'=-H_c^{-1}\nabla K(\theta_c)\) and \(\|H_c^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq h^{-1}\).  Exactly as in the integral inequality
\[
 \|\theta_c\|\leq\frac Lh\int_{c_0}^c\|\theta_s\|\,ds
\]
and its reversed-limit counterpart, differentiating the exponentially weighted integral proves \(\theta_c=0\) on a relative neighborhood of \(c_0\).  Continuity makes the zero set closed, so its being also relatively open in the interval \(\mathcal C\) implies that it is empty or all of \(\mathcal C\).  Nonconstancy rules out the latter; therefore \(\theta_c\neq0\) for every \(c\).

For any such \(c\), set \(\theta=\theta_c\).  Direct differentiation of the finite softmax sum gives, with
\[
 \ell_x(t)=\log\sum_a b_a(x)e^{t\theta^\top q_a(x)},
\]
the identity
\[
 \frac d{dt}\left\{t\ell_x'(t)-\ell_x(t)\right\}
 =t\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_{t\theta}}
   \{\theta^\top q_A(x)\mid X=x\}.
\]
Feature identification gives a \(\delta>0\) and an event \(E\) of positive \(P_X\)-probability on which
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\theta}
   \{\theta^\top q_A(X)\mid X\}\geq2\delta.
\]
For any sequence of positive difference-quotient increments decreasing to zero, pointwise convergence lets one increase measurable subsets of \(E\) to \(E\) on which every sufficiently late quotient is at least \(\delta\).  Integrating on those subsets and using countable additivity gives
\[
 \theta^\top g_c\geq\delta P_X(E)>0.
\]
Thus \(g_c\neq0\).  Since \(H_c\) is positive definite, \(g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c>0\) for every \(c\).  Smoothness and continuity of \(\theta_c\) make \(g_c\) and \(H_c\) continuous, and the curvature floor makes inversion continuous.  Compactness of \(\mathcal C\) therefore gives
\[
 \kappa_K:=\min_{c\in\mathcal C}g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c>0,
\]
which proves the uniform derivative assertion.

For \(c<t\), integration gives
\[
 K(\theta_t)-K(\theta_c)
 =-\int_c^t g_s^\top H_s^{-1}g_s\,ds
 \leq-\kappa_K(t-c)<0.                                         \tag{19}
\]
Hence the continuous map \(c\mapsto K(\theta_c)\) takes \(\mathcal C\) bijectively onto \([K_{\min},K_{\max}]\), with the stated reversed endpoint conventions.  Its inverse is continuous: if \(k_j\to k\), compactness gives a convergent subsequence of \(c(k_j)\), and continuity plus injectivity forces every such subsequential limit to equal \(c(k)\).  Continuity implies Borel measurability.  Inequality (19), with \(c=c(k)\) and \(t=c(\widetilde k)\) in the appropriate order, gives the displayed Lipschitz bound.  For interior \(k\), division of
\[
 K(\theta_{c(k+u)})-K(\theta_{c(k)})=u
\]
by \(c(k+u)-c(k)\), followed by \(u\to0\), yields
\[
 c'(k)=\{K'(c(k))\}^{-1}
 =-\{g_{c(k)}^\top H_{c(k)}^{-1}g_{c(k)}\}^{-1}.
\]
The clipped extension is continuous at both endpoints by the endpoint conventions and is therefore measurable.  Finally, the continuous inverse maps a compact interior divergence interval to a compact set; strict endpoint ordering keeps that image inside \((c_{\min},c_{\max})\).
body.justification: This lemma records the directive's stronger conclusion: pointwise feature identification and compact path continuity yield a positive uniform derivative bound, a unique measurable population inverse, endpoint conventions, and a Lipschitz inverse on the whole attainable range.
body.gap: Fixed-preference analysis does not provide a uniformly regular divergence coordinate for simultaneous inference after selecting a point from the frontier.
body.consumer: It supplies the deterministic inversion and localization step for the fixed-divergence influence expansion and its compact-interior simultaneous band.
